slides.0.title: Great Southern and Tasmania
slides.0.subtitle: Level 1 · Module 5 · Lesson 2
slides.1.title: Great Southern: WA's Vast Cool Region
slides.1.points.0: Location: Southern Western Australia; Australia's largest GI by area
slides.1.points.1: Contains 5 sub-regions: Albany, Denmark, Mount Barker, Frankland River, Porongurup
slides.1.points.2: Climate: cool to cold maritime — influenced by Southern Ocean
slides.1.points.3: Key varieties: Riesling (Frankland River), Shiraz (Mount Barker), Pinot Noir + Chardonnay (Porongurup, Denmark)
slides.1.points.4: Character: purity, freshness, cool-climate restraint — contrasts sharply with warm WA inland regions
slides.2.title: Tasmania: Australia's Coolest Wine Region
slides.2.points.0: Location: island state 240 km south of mainland; closest to Antarctica
slides.2.points.1: Climate: cool-maritime; average temperature 10°C lower than Barossa — best cool-climate wines
slides.2.points.2: Key varieties: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Riesling, plus world-class sparkling wine base
slides.2.points.3: Two regions: Tamar Valley / Pipers River (north, sparkling-focused) + Coal River / Derwent (south, Pinot-focused)
slides.2.points.4: Sparkling: Pipers River is the birthplace of premium Australian sparkling — House of Arras, Jansz
slides.3.title: Why Tasmania is the Future of Premium Australian Wine
slides.3.points.0: As Australia warms due to climate change, Tasmania's cool climate becomes more valuable
slides.3.points.1: Champagne houses (Louis Roederer, Moët & Chandon) are already sourcing from TAS or investing there
slides.3.points.2: Tolpuddle Vineyard (Coal River): world-class Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from Shaw + Smith
slides.3.points.3: Moorilla (MONA museum winery, Derwent Valley): boutique, biodynamic, critically acclaimed
slides.3.points.4: House of Arras sparkling: multiple World's Best Sparkling Wine awards
slides.4.question: Why are major Champagne houses now investing in or sourcing from Tasmania?
slides.4.options.1: Climate change is making traditional Champagne regions warmer, and Tasmania's cool maritime climate can produce the high-acid, delicate base wines needed for world-class sparkling
slides.4.options.2: Tasmania has lower taxes on wine production
slides.4.options.3: Tasmanian grapes look identical to Champagne varieties
slides.4.explanation: As global temperatures rise, the Champagne region faces challenges maintaining the high natural acidity essential for fine sparkling wine. Tasmania — with its cool Southern Ocean climate and long slow-ripening season — offers an ideal alternative. Houses like Louis Roederer have recognised this, and many Australian sparkling wine producers use Tasmanian fruit for their premium cuvées.
slides.5.title: Lesson Summary
slides.5.points.0: Great Southern: WA's largest GI; 5 sub-regions; cool-climate Riesling (Frankland), Shiraz (Mt Barker), Pinot (Porongurup)
slides.5.points.1: Tasmania: Australia's coolest region; world-class sparkling (House of Arras, Jansz) + elegant Pinot Noir
slides.5.points.2: TAS is Australia's future luxury wine region — Champagne houses already investing here
